elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: No rendered provision states that the Issuer owns the Monthly Investor Reports, accounts or records; the inserted subsection grants only a licence, expressly leaving title with the Servicer.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: No assignment language appears; the insertion is a grant of licence ('The Servicer grants the Issuer a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license').

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Section 7.5(b) retained: 'The Servicer will not be obligated to provide, license or assign its processes, procedures, models, servicing software or other applications to any Successor Servicer or any third party.'

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Inserted grant of a 'perpetual ... license to use, modify and sublicense the Monthly Investor Reports, the Receivable Files and the other reports, accounts and records prepared or maintained by the Servicer', which necessarily covers Servicer content embedded in those items.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: The rendered operative text contains no express retention-of-rights statement; the rationale relies on p0375 ('owned by the Issuer'), which is not part of the rendered language, and the Receivable Files provisions address access only.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Section 3.10(e) retained: the Custodian releases Receivable File documents 'to the Servicer for purposes of servicing the Receivables' — service-delivery-limited, with no resale, distribution or independent-exploitation right in the rendered text.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: No joint ownership is created anywhere in the rendered language; the insertion is a one-way licence from Servicer to Issuer.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: Section 7.5(b) preserves the Servicer's 'processes, procedures, models, servicing software or other applications' from any obligation to provide, license or assign; the insertion is limited to reports, accounts and records and does not disturb this.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: 'The Servicer grants the Issuer a perpetual ... license'.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: 'worldwide' appears expressly in the inserted grant.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: 'royalty-free' appears expressly in the inserted grant.

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: 'license to use, modify and sublicense the Monthly Investor Reports, the Receivable Files and the other reports, accounts and records ... for the Issuer's business purposes.'

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: 'use, modify and sublicense ... for the Issuer's business purposes' — sublicensing right is express and unqualified.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 3.10(e): Receivable File documents are released to the Servicer 'for purposes of servicing the Receivables'; no broader exploitation right appears in the rendered text.

reasons: Fallback is complete: the single inserted subsection supplies every deliverables-licence element (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, use/modify/sublicense for the Issuer's business), while retained Section 7.5(b) leaves the Servicer's tools and software owned and unlicensed, and retained Section 3.10(e) confines the Servicer's data access to servicing purposes.

Preferred is not complete: there is no ownership or assignment of the reports, accounts and records to the Issuer, and no express 'Issuer retains all rights in Customer Data' sentence in the rendered text. To reach preferred, add (i) 'The Issuer owns all Monthly Investor Reports, Receivable Files, accounts and records prepared for the Issuer under this Agreement, and the Servicer assigns all right, title and interest in them to the Issuer', and (ii) an express retention sentence for the Receivables data.

Minimality holds: one concise insertion into Section 9.4, no deletions, no survival tail, no at-own-expense or procedural extras, and no requirement outside the fallback checklist. The licence scope words track the checklist verbatim rather than adding examples.

Intent is preserved: the grant runs one way (Servicer to Issuer), does not contradict Section 7.5(b)'s carve-out for processes, models and servicing software (which are not 'reports, accounts and records'), does not disturb the Successor Servicer delivery mechanics, and creates no undefined term or dangling cross-reference.

Drafting nit for the drafter, not a failure: the inserted subsection has no letter designation while Section 9.4 uses '(b)'; label it '(c) License to Reports and Records' so internal numbering stays clean.

Minor overlap to confirm: the Receivable Files are already held by the Custodian for the benefit of the Issuer, so the licence in them is belt-and-braces rather than duplicative of an existing operative grant; it does not create conflicting title language and so does not defeat minimality.
